message.content:
**Roast Five Whole Chickens – A Simple Yet Delicious Family‑Style Meal** > *This recipe yields about **5–7 servings per chicken**, so you’ll have plenty left over for lunch tomorrow!* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Quantity | |------|----------| | Fresh whole chickens (about 2 lb / 900 g each) | 5 | | Olive oil or melted butter | ½ cup (120 ml) | | Salt | 2 tsp (10 g) + extra for rubbing inside cavities | | Black pepper | 1 tsp (5 g) | | Garlic cloves, minced | 8–10 | | Lemon halves | 5 | | Fresh herbs (rosemary, thyme, sage) | ¼ cup chopped (or 5 sprigs each) | | Onion, quartered | 5 | | Carrots & celery sticks | 10 sticks total | | Optional: paprika, cayenne, smoked salt | pinch each | *Feel free to swap out herbs or spices according to your taste.* --- ### Equipment Needed - Large baking tray or roasting pan (big enough to hold all five chickens without crowding) - Kitchen twine (for trussing) - Meat thermometer (instant-read) --- #### Step‑by‑Step Instructions | # | Action | Notes | |---|--------|-------| | 1 | **Pre‑heat Oven** | Set to **425 °F (220 °C)**. If your oven runs hot, lower it slightly to avoid burning the skin. | | 2 | **Prepare Chickens** | • Pat dry with paper towels.
• Remove giblets from cavities (save for stock if desired).
• Season generously both outside and inside with salt, pepper, garlic, lemon zest, and fresh herbs.
• Stuff each cavity with one half‑lemon, some herb stems, and a few onion quarters. | | 3 | **Truss Legs** | Tie the legs together with kitchen twine to keep the shape while roasting. | | 4 | **Oil/Baste** | Brush each bird with olive oil or melted butter—this helps crisp the skin. | | 5 | **Arrange on Tray** | Place chickens breast‑side up, spaced evenly. Add carrots/celery around them for natural steam and flavor. | | 6 | **First Roast Phase** | Bake for **30 min** at 425 °F. Then reduce heat to **375 °F (190 °C)**. | | 7 | **Second Roast Phase** | Continue roasting for another **45–60 min** (total approx. 75–90 min). Use a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of thigh (avoid bone); target **165 °F (74 °C)**. | | 8 | **Rest Time** | Once done, remove from oven and tent loosely with foil. Let rest **15–20 min** before carving. Rest allows juices to redistribute, keeping meat moist. | | 9 | **Carve & Serve** | Slice off breasts first, then carve drumsticks/thighs. Plate alongside roasted veggies, mashed potatoes, or a simple green salad. | |10 | **Optional Gravy** | While resting, place the roasting pan on stovetop, pour in a splash of white wine or broth, scrape up browned bits, simmer until reduced, strain, season, and serve. | --- ### Quick Cooking‑Time Calculator (If You Want Exact Numbers) If you'd prefer precise timing based on actual weight: ```python from functions import recipe_calculator_calculate_time recipe_calculator_calculate_time({ "weight": 0.9, # average weight per chicken in kilograms "per_unit_time": 12, # minutes per kilogram (typical roasting rule) }) ``` *(Replace `weight` with the exact mass of each chicken.)* --- ### Tips & Variations | Tip | Why It Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Brine** | Soak chickens in salted water (1 tbsp salt per quart) for 1–2 hrs before roasting to lock moisture. | | **Spice Rub** | Mix paprika, cumin, coriander, and brown sugar for a sweet‑smoky crust. | | **Low‑Heat Finish** | After initial high‑temp sear, finish at 300 °F (150 °C) for even doneness. | | **Stuffings** | Try stuffing with apples, onions, or rice for added flavor. | | **Leftovers** | Store leftovers in airtight containers; reheat gently in microwave or skillet. | Enjoy this hearty meal that’s perfect for family gatherings, potlucks, or simply feeding a big group. Bon appétit!
